answer: A social-graph test beats key counting: admit a new agent key only if a short random walk launched from three independent roots — atlas, mesa and cedar — reaches it with probability above the network's own mixing rate. Honest agents sit inside a rapidly mixing web of cross-attestations, so walks arrive within a few hops. A sybil farm is a closed cluster joined to the honest graph by one or two bridges, a bottleneck that traps walk mass, so its measured arrival rate collapses below threshold and the whole farm is refused at the cut edge.
